Theme token reference

Contribute to this guideShow the table of contents

This page lists the foundation tokens and the semantic tokens of the CKEditor 5 UI theme. These are the CSS variables that you override most often:

  • Foundation tokens are the raw values of the theme: the color palette, such as --ck-color-base-action, and the scales, such as the spacing steps --ck-spacing-sm and --ck-spacing-md. Override them for a broad change, such as a new brand color or a denser UI.
  • Semantic tokens name a design role shared by many components, such as the background of a panel or the focus ring of a control. Override them to change one role across the whole UI, or to fine-tune the result of a broad change.

The Theme customization guide explains how to choose a layer and where to set an override.

The list is generated from the theme source files at every documentation build, so it always matches the theme of this version. The component tokens are not on this page.

How to read the list

Copy link

Each row shows the name of a token, the first sentence of its description, and its value in the default theme, with a preview. The details of a row hold the rest of the description, the default value as the theme declares it, the value that it resolves to, the tokens that it follows and that follow it, and the contrast pairs.

The steps of a scale, such as --ck-spacing-sm, have no description of their own. The description of their file, above their rows, explains the whole scale and, when the scale has one, the token that resizes it, such as --ck-spacing-base.

On the page, the filter above the list matches the names, the descriptions, and the values. A row must contain every word that you type, so surface overlay finds the tokens that mention both words.

Token chains

Copy link

Most tokens read the value of another token. The details show this chain in both directions:

  • Follows names the tokens that the token reads. A legacy name or a deprecated alias in between is skipped, so the list names the token to override.
  • Followed by names the tokens on this page whose default declaration on :root reads the token, directly or through other tokens. They change when you override the token on :root. An override on a narrower selector does not change them, because the theme resolves them on :root. The Theme customization guide explains global and scoped overrides.

Check Followed by when you plan a broad change. One brand color is often spread over several foundation colors. For example, --ck-color-base-action colors the primary buttons, --ck-color-base-active colors the accent text and the text of the toggled-on buttons, and --ck-color-base-focus colors the focus rings. Override all of them, together with their variants, such as --ck-color-base-action-hover. Some semantic colors do not follow any foundation color, so a new brand color does not change them. For example, the pulsing glow of the buttons that insert a paragraph next to a widget comes from --ck-color-interactive-focus-border-coordinates, which holds the default focus color as fixed values. Override such tokens too.

A scale can follow another scale. The widths of panels, such as --ck-width-md, grow with the font size, so Followed by of --ck-font-size-base lists them too, and a new font size also resizes the panels. The focus tokens of the foundation, such as --ck-focus-shadow, read semantic tokens, such as --ck-color-interactive-focus-shadow, so their Follows points to the semantic layer.

Followed by lists only the tokens on this page, and it traces only their declarations on :root. The components and other tokens of the theme can read a token as well, so a token without Followed by is not necessarily unused. A token that the theme declares again under another selector can depend on more tokens there. For example, --ck-radius-corners reads --ck-radius-base inside .ck-rounded-corners, so a new base radius changes it too, although Followed by of --ck-radius-base does not list it. Its description explains this.

Contrast pairs

Copy link

A contrast pair names the content drawn on a background token, such as text or icons. If you change a background, check the contrast of each of its pairs too. The theme marks a pair on the background token only, as described in the Contrast pairs section of the Theme token naming guide. This page shows it on both tokens: the background lists its pairs under Contrast pairs, and the content token lists its backgrounds under Used on.

The page computes the contrast ratio of every pair in the default theme. A translucent background is first composited over the canvas color, --ck-color-surface-canvas. The ratios are rounded down, so the page never shows a ratio higher than it is.

A pair does not tell what its content is, such as text, an icon, or a decoration, so the page shows the ratio without a verdict. Compare it with the minimum for the content. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines require 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text in Contrast (Minimum), and 3:1 for icons, borders, and other parts of the UI that you need to see to use it in Non-text Contrast.

If the page cannot read a color of a pair, for example a color that is not hsl(), it shows contrast not computed instead of the ratio.

Deprecated tokens

Copy link

A token marked as deprecated is kept for compatibility, as described in the Deprecated tokens section of the Theme token naming guide. The theme still declares it, but new code and new overrides should use the token named in its details under Use instead. Being deprecated does not mean that the token will be removed.

No tokens match the filter.

Spacing

Copy link

Source: _spacing.css

The spacing scale of the editor UI. Set --ck-spacing-base on :root to resize every step. To change the spacing of one group of elements, such as controls, override its semantic spacing role, such as --ck-spacing-control-padding-inline, instead.

The change color roles of the editor: the colors that mark an insertion, a deletion, or a format change when changes are suggested or compared, and the accent of comment annotations. To change one kind of change across the editor, override its role. To change one component, override its component token instead. The markers are drawn over the edited content, which takes the text color of the page, so the text on them has no @pair.

The typography roles of the editor UI: the font weights of kinds of UI text, and the font sizes of controls and of toolbar labels. To change one kind of text across the UI, override its role, such as --ck-font-weight-ui-heading. To change one component, override its component token instead. These roles do not change the edited content.

Spacing

Copy link

Source: _semantic-spacing.css

The spacing roles of the editor UI: the padding of controls, and the padding and gap tiers that components pick their spacing from. To change the padding of controls across the UI, override a control role, such as --ck-spacing-control-padding-inline. The padding and gap tiers set a density, not a purpose: a component token names the purpose and reads a tier, such as --ck-toolbar-padding: 0 var(--ck-spacing-padding-compact), so overriding a tier changes every component that reads it. To change the spacing of one component, override its component token instead.

Sizes

Copy link

Source: _semantic-width.css

The width roles of the editor UI: the widths of balloon forms and dialogs. To change the width of one kind of panel across the UI, such as dialogs, override its role, such as --ck-width-dialog. To change one component, override its component token instead. Set --ck-font-size-base on :root to resize all of them together with the font sizes. Each role is capped at 90% of the viewport width, so the panels fit on narrow screens.

    • Resolves to: min(320px, 90vw)
    • Follows: --ck-width-sm

  • --ck-width-dialog#: Width of dialogs, such as the find and replace dialog and the media embed form.—min(400px, 90vw)

    Details
    • Default: min(var(--ck-width-md), 90vw)
    • Resolves to: min(400px, 90vw)
    • Follows: --ck-width-md

  • --ck-width-dialog-lg#: Width of large dialogs.—min(560px, 90vw)

    Details
    • Default: min(var(--ck-width-xl), 90vw)
    • Resolves to: min(560px, 90vw)
    • Follows: --ck-width-xl

  • --ck-width-dialog-xl#: Width of extra large dialogs.—min(640px, 90vw)

    Details
    • Default: min(var(--ck-width-2xl), 90vw)
    • Resolves to: min(640px, 90vw)
    • Follows: --ck-width-2xl

Source: _semantic-layout.css

The layout roles of the editor UI: the sizes that several components share. To change the size of one component, override its component token instead.

  • --ck-size-control-min-height#: Minimum height of controls, such as buttons and text inputs.32px

    Details · Full description

    Buttons also use it as their minimum width, so an icon button is at least square. Set --ck-font-size-base on :root to resize it together with the font sizes. It is read where controls are drawn, so it can also be set on a part of the UI, as the theme does for small buttons.

    • Default: var(--ck-ui-component-min-height, calc(var(--ck-font-size-normal, var(--ck-font-size-base))*2))
    • Resolves to: 32px
    • Follows: --ck-font-size-base

Layers

Copy link

Source: _semantic-layer.css

The stacking roles of the editor UI: the z-index of controls, panels, dialogs, and tooltips relative to each other. To change the stacking of one group of elements, such as dialogs, override its role, such as --ck-layer-dialog. To move the whole UI relative to the rest of the page, change the z-index scale (--ck-z-base, --ck-z-overlay, and --ck-z-modal) instead.

  • --ck-layer-base#: Base layer of controls, which keeps a focused item, such as a list item, above its neighbors, so that its focus border and focus shadow are not covered.11

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-z-default, var(--ck-z-base))
    • Resolves to: 1
    • Follows: --ck-z-base
    • Followed by:
      • --ck-layer-control-raised
      • --ck-layer-balloon-arrow-back
      • --ck-layer-balloon-arrow-front

  • --ck-layer-control-raised#: Layer of a focused control that must stay above the controls next to it, such as a button in a toolbar dropdown or a split button.22

    Details
    • Default: calc(var(--ck-layer-base) + 1)
    • Resolves to: 2
    • Follows: --ck-layer-base

  • --ck-layer-panel#: Layer of floating panels, such as balloons, dropdown panels, and the sticky toolbar.10001000

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-z-panel, var(--ck-z-overlay))
    • Resolves to: 1000
    • Follows: --ck-z-overlay
    • Followed by:
      • --ck-layer-panel-above
      • --ck-layer-panel-below

  • --ck-layer-panel-above#: Layer of a panel that must stand above other panels, such as the panel of a dropdown in a toolbar or the panel of a dropdown menu.10011001

    Details
    • Default: calc(var(--ck-layer-panel) + 1)
    • Resolves to: 1001
    • Follows: --ck-layer-panel

  • --ck-layer-panel-below#: Layer of the fake panels that show a stack of balloons under the visible one.999999

    Details
    • Default: calc(var(--ck-layer-panel) - 1)
    • Resolves to: 999
    • Follows: --ck-layer-panel

  • --ck-layer-dialog#: Layer of dialogs.99999999

    Details · Full description

    Elements that must stand above dialogs, such as the emoji picker, the mention list, and CKBox in the fullscreen mode, use one layer above it.

    • Default: var(--ck-z-dialog, var(--ck-z-modal))
    • Resolves to: 9999
    • Follows: --ck-z-modal
    • Followed by:
      • --ck-layer-tooltip

  • --ck-layer-tooltip#: Layer of tooltips, above every other part of the UI, including dialogs.1009910099

    Details
    • Default: calc(var(--ck-layer-dialog) + 100)
    • Resolves to: 10099
    • Follows: --ck-layer-dialog

  • --ck-layer-balloon-arrow-back#: Layer of the back part of a balloon arrow, its border.-2-2

    Details
    • Default: calc(var(--ck-layer-base) - 3)
    • Resolves to: -2
    • Follows: --ck-layer-base
    • Followed by:
      • --ck-layer-balloon-arrow-front

  • --ck-layer-balloon-arrow-front#: Layer of the front part of a balloon arrow, its fill, drawn over the back part.-1-1

    Details
    • Default: calc(var(--ck-layer-balloon-arrow-back) + 1)
    • Resolves to: -1
    • Follows: --ck-layer-balloon-arrow-back

Motion

Copy link

Source: _semantic-motion.css

The motion roles of the editor UI: the durations and the easing of transitions and animations, by the kind of motion. To change one kind of motion across the UI, such as the transitions of controls, override its role, such as --ck-transition-duration-control. To change one component, override its component token instead.

  • --ck-transition-duration-control-fast#: Duration of quick control transitions, such as the border and the shadow of a text input, and the floating label of a labeled field..1s.1s

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-duration-fast)
    • Resolves to: .1s
    • Follows: --ck-duration-fast
    • Followed by:
      • --ck-transition-control-fast

  • --ck-transition-duration-control#: Duration of control transitions, such as changes of borders and shadows..2s.2s

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-duration-base)
    • Resolves to: .2s
    • Follows: --ck-duration-base
    • Followed by:
      • --ck-transition-control

  • --ck-transition-duration-control-emphasized#: Duration of larger control movements, such as the toggle of a switch button..3s.3s

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-duration-slow)
    • Resolves to: .3s
    • Follows: --ck-duration-slow

  • --ck-transition-duration-surface#: Duration of transitions of surfaces, which change more than controls and take longer..4s.4s

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-duration-slower)
    • Resolves to: .4s
    • Follows: --ck-duration-slower

  • --ck-transition-timing-function-control#: Easing of control transitions, such as the border and the shadow of a button.—ease-in-out

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-ease-interactive)
    • Resolves to: ease-in-out
    • Follows: --ck-ease-interactive
    • Followed by:
      • --ck-transition-control
      • --ck-transition-control-fast

  • --ck-transition-timing-function-control-emphasized#: Easing of emphasized control movements, such as the floating label of a labeled field.—cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.24, 0.95)

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-ease-emphasized)
    • Resolves to: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.24, 0.95)
    • Follows: --ck-ease-emphasized

  • --ck-transition-timing-function-surface#: Easing of surface transitions, such as the background of a switch button.—ease

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-ease-standard)
    • Resolves to: ease
    • Follows: --ck-ease-standard

  • --ck-transition-control#: Transition of the shadow and the border of a control, such as a button.—box-shadow .2s ease-in-out, border .2s ease-in-out

    Details · Full description

    Use it as the whole value of transition.

    • Default: box-shadow var(--ck-transition-duration-control) var(--ck-transition-timing-function-control), border var(--ck-transition-duration-control) var(--ck-transition-timing-function-control)
    • Resolves to: box-shadow .2s ease-in-out, border .2s ease-in-out
    • Follows: --ck-transition-duration-control, --ck-transition-timing-function-control

  • --ck-transition-control-fast#: Quick transition of the shadow and the border of a control, such as a text input.—box-shadow .1s ease-in-out, border .1s ease-in-out

    Details · Full description

    Use it as the whole value of transition.

    • Default: box-shadow var(--ck-transition-duration-control-fast) var(--ck-transition-timing-function-control), border var(--ck-transition-duration-control-fast) var(--ck-transition-timing-function-control)
    • Resolves to: box-shadow .1s ease-in-out, border .1s ease-in-out
    • Follows: --ck-transition-duration-control-fast, --ck-transition-timing-function-control

  • --ck-animation-duration-feedback#: Duration of feedback animations, such as the shake of a text input with an error..3s.3s

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-animation-duration-slow)
    • Resolves to: .3s
    • Follows: --ck-animation-duration-slow

  • --ck-animation-duration-surface-entrance#: Duration of the animation of a surface that appears, such as the fade-in of a dialog..3s.3s

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-animation-duration-slow)
    • Resolves to: .3s
    • Follows: --ck-animation-duration-slow

  • --ck-animation-duration-progress#: Duration of one cycle of a progress animation, such as the rotation of a spinner.1.5s1.5s

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-animation-duration-emphasis)
    • Resolves to: 1.5s
    • Follows: --ck-animation-duration-emphasis

  • --ck-animation-duration-progress-reduced#: Duration of one cycle of a progress animation when the user prefers reduced motion.0s0s

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-animation-duration-reduced)
    • Resolves to: 0s
    • Follows: --ck-animation-duration-reduced

  • --ck-animation-timing-function-feedback#: Easing of feedback animations, such as the shake of a text input with an error.—ease

    Details
    • Default: var(--ck-animation-ease-standard)
    • Resolves to: ease
    • Follows: --ck-animation-ease-standard

  • --ck-animation-timing-function-progress#: Easing of progress animations, such as the rotation of a spinner.—linear

    Details · Full description

    Keep it linear, so that a looping animation keeps an even speed.

    • Default: var(--ck-animation-ease-linear)
